import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load data
print("Loading data...")
train = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_test_2.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_sample_submission_2.csv")

print(f"Train shape: {train.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test.shape}")
print(f"Sample submission shape: {sample_sub.shape}")

# Create validation split from training data BEFORE building mapping (to avoid contamination)
print("Creating validation split for evaluation...")
np.random.seed(42)
all_indices = np.arange(len(train))
np.random.shuffle(all_indices)

# Use 80% for training, 20% for validation - the validation fold is never used to build the mapping
split_idx = int(0.8 * len(train))
train_fold = train.iloc[np.array(all_indices[:split_idx])]
val_fold = train.iloc[np.array(all_indices[split_idx:])]

print(f"Train fold size: {len(train_fold)}")
print(f"Validation fold size: {len(val_fold)}")

# Build most frequent mapping using ONLY train_fold (WITHOUT class information for consistency)
print(
    "Building token normalization mapping from train_fold (using before only for consistency)..."
)
exact_mappings = {}
count_dict = {}
for _, row in train_fold.iterrows():
    if pd.notna(row["before"]) and pd.notna(row["after"]):
        before = str(row["before"])
        after = str(row["after"])
        # Use (before,) only for consistent key space between train and test
        if before not in exact_mappings:
            exact_mappings[before] = []
        exact_mappings[before].append(after)

# For each before, keep the most frequent 'after'
final_mapping = {}
for key, afters in exact_mappings.items():
    counter = Counter(afters)
    final_mapping[key] = counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

print(f"Total unique mappings: {len(final_mapping)}")

# Test the mapping on validation fold (proper hold-out evaluation with consistent keys)
print("Validating mapping on hold-out set...")
val_preds = []
val_true = []
for _, row in val_fold.iterrows():
    before = str(row["before"])
    after = str(row["after"])
    # Use before as fallback for unmapped tokens (more appropriate than 'sil' for normalization)
    pred = final_mapping.get(before, before)
    val_preds.append(pred)
    val_true.append(after)

# Calculate accuracy - this is now a genuine hold-out metric with consistent key space
correct = sum(1 for p, t in zip(val_preds, val_true) if p == t)
accuracy = correct / len(val_true) if len(val_true) > 0 else 0.0
print(f"Validation accuracy (hold-out): {accuracy:.6f}")
print(f"Correct: {correct}/{len(val_true)}")
print(f"Error examples (first 10 mismatches):")
for p, t in zip(val_preds, val_true):
    if p != t:
        print(f"  before={t[:20]}, pred={p[:20]}, true={t[:20]}")
        if len([x for x in zip(val_preds, val_true) if x[0] != x[1]]) >= 10:
            break

# Generate predictions for test set using the SAME mapping (test has no class column)
print("Generating predictions for test set...")
test["id"] = test["sentence_id"].astype(str) + "_" + test["token_id"].astype(str)
# Apply mapping with before as fallback for unmapped tokens
test["after"] = test["before"].apply(lambda x: final_mapping.get(str(x), str(x)))

# Ensure correct submission format
submission = test[["id", "after"]].copy()
submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv with {len(submission)} rows")
print(f"Submission columns: {submission.columns.tolist()}")
print(f"Sample submission:\n{submission.head()}")
print(f"\nFinal validation accuracy (hold-out): {accuracy:.6f}")
plan: The previous solution builds mappings using (before, class) tuples, but test data lacks class information and defaults to 'PLAIN', creating a mismatch. I will improve this by building mappings using only (before,) tuples consistently for both training and test, ensuring test predictions use the same key space as validation. Additionally, I will use the original token text as a fallback when a mapping key is not found, which is more appropriate for text normalization where unmapped tokens should remain unchanged rather than becoming 'sil'.
